## Objective
Implement a declared-assumption MinTRL estimator that reports the minimum observation horizon needed to distinguish a target Sharpe at a stated confidence and power.

## Owning authority
- D-153 statistical triple and Rule 12.
- V8_Profesyonel_Benchmark_Arastirmasi.pdf, MinTRL section.
- docs/contracts/D153_BENCHMARK_FABRIC_SPEC.md
- Bailey and Lopez de Prado DSR assumptions as a related statistical authority.

## Change class
BENCHMARK_EVALUATION

## Current state / Null hypothesis
No MinTRL implementation or named estimator appears in v8-next. The current benchmark reports Sharpe and confidence intervals, while short historical windows are merely labeled underpowered.

## Required end state / Challenger hypothesis
H1 — Given a preregistered target Sharpe, null Sharpe, confidence, power, dependence model, interval unit, and variance assumptions, the estimator returns a reproducible required horizon. H0 — if assumptions or data are missing, it returns UNDERPOWERED/UNSUPPORTED rather than a universal trade-count or calendar threshold.

## Expected file / module surface
v8-next/src/v8_next/evaluation/mintrl.py (new)
v8-next/src/v8_next/evaluation/inference.py
v8-next/src/v8_next/evaluation/economic_benchmark.py
v8-next/tests/test_mintrl.py (new)
v8-next/tests/test_inference.py

## Verification gates
Verify analytic cases against independently calculated reference values, unit/annualization semantics, dependence and power sensitivity, invalid/degenerate inputs, and deterministic serialization. Run only on real aligned return intervals for economic reporting.

## Required evidence artifacts
Versioned MinTRL plan; formula/assumption receipt; input interval manifest; estimator output; underpowered/error receipt; independent test evidence.

## Non-goals / forbidden scope
No fixed universal threshold, no hardcoded p-values/effect sizes, no synthetic production outcomes, no conversion of MinTRL into a profitability or capital decision.

### Context-completeness contract

### 11. Normative Traceability
R1 — Target, null, alpha/confidence, power, variance and dependence assumptions are explicit. Authority: PDF MinTRL limits.
R2 — Output is horizon evidence, not a strategy pass. Authority: Rule 12.
R3 — Missing assumptions fail closed.

### 12. Existing Types / Interfaces to Reuse
Reuse IntervalLoss, alignment chronology, existing estimator-version binding, scipy/numpy dependency identity, and NO_ECONOMIC_CLAIM status vocabulary.

### 13. Mathematical / Semantic Invariants
I1: changing interval unit or annualization changes the identity.
I2: missing variance/dependence/power inputs never become zero/default.
I3: required horizon is monotone under the declared model, subject to explicit numerical bounds.

### 14. Canonical Failure Semantics
Missing assumptions -> UNSUPPORTED.
Insufficient observations -> UNDERPOWERED.
Nonfinite/degenerate input -> DATA_BLOCKED or BLOCKED.
Computed value without authority -> NO_ECONOMIC_CLAIM.

### 15. Dependency Map
Plan -> aligned returns -> MinTRL estimator -> method receipt -> descriptive report; no path to capital authority.

### 16. Ambiguity / OPEN_PIN Triggers
- If the estimand, authority, or data role is ambiguous, STOP and open an OPEN_PIN.
- If the required source data is unavailable, report DATA_BLOCKED; do not manufacture observations.
- If a result could be interpreted as an economic claim, keep it NO_ECONOMIC_CLAIM.

### References / sources / attachments
Related: #322. MinTRL is specifically absent from v8-next even though the older v8-core Minerva path mentions it.

### V8 guards
- [x] I will not fabricate, hardcode, or synthesize statistical metrics.
- [x] Constitution Rule 12 (NO_ECONOMIC_CLAIM) remains binding without certified authority receipts.
- [x] Frozen OOS will not be opened without explicit pre-authorization.
- [x] If statistical methodology or data authority is ambiguous, I will open/escalate an OPEN_PIN.
